pitch_detail.notes: A long traverse across spray-cone ice to reach the bolted belay, using roughly four to six ice screws. This pitch is a way in rather than the main event.

The main pitch. Step right on spray ice from the belay, then climb a dry overhanging torquing corner with diagonal columnar features and orange lichen. Stems and knee bars lead to the first of three dagger and ice-roof systems; pull under, around and through the next two, each bigger than the last. Chimney behind the main dagger and finish up ice petals to the bolted belay. Expect about 18 quickdraws and long runners, plus 2-3 screws if some bolts are buried in ice.

The exit shared with the neighbouring route. Difficulty ranges from WI4/M4 up to M5/6 depending on conditions. Go right on mixed ground past the old belay, which is too exposed to overhead fall to use. Work upward by stemming across the gap between the ice strand and the steep wall, resting on good stances; clip bolts out left, or place screws where the ice is sound; roughly 5 bolts and/or 4-8 screws. Above the lip, follow ice or moss beside the creek to trees at the observation deck. Pitches 2 and 3 can likely be linked on an 80 m rope with a rope switch and roller draws, avoiding the second hanging belay.

pitch_detail.notes: A narrow ice flow in a shallow dihedral in the middle of the slab, below the vertical wall. The slab often holds snow, which makes the easiest line hard to follow. Some parties skip it by walking the snow to the left and back right to the foot of the second pitch.

pitch_detail.anchor: birch tree with slings and rap rings
pitch_detail.notes: Ice features lead you to the foot of the steep, intricate upper part. The upper part is balancy, changes from season to season, and requires manoeuvring onto a steep column; protection is probably better higher up, but the pitch is serious. Belay from a birch tree with slings and rap rings, a few metres left of the step.

review.changed: 2 pitches with stated lengths/grades. No rappel stations listed.

pitch_detail.notes: A thick pitch of ice that offers several line options.
Easy ground: follow the river upstream to the main waterfall. Can be soloed.
Steep ice with several line options on the main waterfall.

review.changed: 3 pitches with notes only; the text gives no grades, lengths or anchors per pitch so none written.

pitch_detail.notes: Vertical sections with good rests between them. Belay on ice screws.
A long slab with a lot of snow lying over ice. Belay on ice screws.
The best pitch, with excellent exposure and many line options ranging from WI3+ to WI5. Belay at trees.

review.changed: 3 pitches with lengths and anchors. Descent is by rappel off trees and Abalakov threads but no stations listed so no table. P3 grade is a range, kept in notes.

pitch_detail.notes: Start left of a roof about 7 feet up. Climb a series of vertical blocks until you pass a pine, then a slab to a cedar. Belay there, or continue right to the start of the roof and build a gear belay.

Follow the crack under the roof leftward, then step onto the block at its end, which moves, so treat it with care. Footholds are scarce on the traverse and the hardest moves come right at the start. Cross the face rightward on the horizontal crack to a belay near a small tree. The crack under the roof takes gear but can be run out in places.
Climb the crack for a little over 5 m, then cross the horizontal crack to reach the top.

review.changed: 3 pitches with grades and lengths. Descent is by rappel from trees on the left with two 60 m ropes; no station list so no table.

pitch_detail.notes: Well protected climbing. Build the belay on gear.
Mostly protected (PG). Belay on gear near a juniper.
Traverse right along an almost horizontal crack. Protection is mostly adequate (PG), and there is a lot of loose rock on this pitch. Belay at a big cedar.

pitch_detail.anchor: tree at the top of the wall
pitch_detail.notes: Head straight up, then pass left under a roof. The pitch is runout in sections (R). Belay at a tree at the top of the cliff.

review.changed: 4 pitches with grades, lengths, anchors. Descent by two rappels with 2x60 m ropes or the hiking trail; no stations, no table.
review.other_findings: Pitch lengths sum to 115 m versus stored length_m 110 (minor).

pitch_detail.notes: Climb a thinly protected face to a ledge.
Trend left up a rising ramp, force a way through the face, then move up and right as far as possible along the ramp of the neighbouring route.
Scramble up and left to the foot of the buttress. Belay at the base of clean vertical cracks.
Take the leftmost crack, a dihedral, and stop at a ramp belay just short of where the cracks open into a chimney. A very good pitch.
Protect the chimney by draping slings over its big chockstones.

The crux is an off-finger crack on the face; after it come a chimney, a small roof and further cracks, ending on a very large wooded ledge. The crux is short, well protected, and easily aided at 5.8 A1.

review.changed: 6 pitches with grades and lengths. Descent is to rappel the route, no stations listed so no table.

pitch_detail.notes: Climb the Coulée Ricard and continue up the gully above. Belay at trees.
Continue through a small patch of forest toward the ice on the left, where a little dihedral with a slim vein of ice begins.
Climb the dihedral holding a thin streak of ice. Try not to break the ice, since it stops forming early in the season. Belay on glue-in bolts at the top.

Low-angle slabby ground up a big weakness left of a neighbouring route, with good turf placements and fun stemming but little protection. It leads to a steep chimney full of large blocks. Clip a pin and traverse right on steep positive holds, pass a second pin, then mantel up onto the slab; long runners make this easier. Belay needs two Lost Arrow pitons and small cams.
Step left off the belay and traverse into a small gully. Climb turf and ice up, then back right on slabby ground to a belay that takes finger-sized cams.
A few bouldery moves lead into Center Chute, then moderate snow. From here the route continues unroped up about 500 ft of steep snow and a short AI2/3 section to the ridge.

review.changed: 3 pitches written. The unroped snow above and the East Ridge 4th-class descent are in the notes only. No rappels.

pitch_detail.notes: Scramble easy ground in the corner; the first piece goes in a 4-inch crack. Shuffle left to a crack system in the middle of the face, then left again onto the arete. Cracks and good holds lead to the belay at a stainless bolt with a button head, with a second bolt just above. A 2-bolt rap anchor serves to descend this pitch to the north.
Crosses the upper horizontal break in a long traverse. The line is illogical-looking but works on the rock. Descent from here is as for the neighbouring route.

review.changed: 2 pitches, no grades or lengths in the text so none written. Rappels are mentioned only generally, no table.

pitch_detail.notes: The start is the tree at the foot of the tower. Work up the left-hand flake onto the tower's left side, then follow a row of pitons in a thin crack for about 50 ft. Below the roof, move back onto the south face, clipping two pitons right under the roof and placing a key 0.75 cam in the vertical crack that splits it. Extend three of the pitons to reduce rope drag under the roof crux. Two-bolt anchor at the top; a good stance partway up the second block above the first roof lets a 70 m rope cover the day.

Splitter hand cracks, another pin ladder, a small roof move and slabby climbing lead to the two-bolt anchor on top of the tower, with a single bolt on the slab just below the top-out. If setting up a top rope, extend the anchor so it clears the lip, otherwise the rope drags or sticks. One long rappel from the top is tempting but ropes often get stuck.

review.changed: 2 pitches written; lengths and grades not stated per pitch (the 50 ft is only the lower section) so omitted. Rappels not listed station by station.

pitch_detail.notes: Climb right-facing flakes to a hand crack on the face, then a splitter corner to the chains. The hand crack is steep with great feet. A crack transfer leads to the short corner below the anchor, which is the crux, with tight hands and fingers.
Traverse left along a ledge, climb cracks into a stem box, then a hand crack through two roofs to the top of the ridge.

review.changed: 2 pitches, no per-pitch grades or lengths given.

pitch_detail.notes: Climb a steep left-facing corner. Near its end there is a fixed pin; move slightly right and belay.
Easier low-angle cracks lead up and right to a good belay ledge.
Short left-facing corners lead to a belay on a sloping ledge.
From the sloping ledge, climb out right to a wide crack that runs to the top of the buttress. This pitch can feel runout; a #5 cam adds confidence.

review.changed: 4 pitches with grades. Details may be slightly off per the text. Descent not tabulated.

pitch_detail.anchor: boulder with webbing and a rap ring
pitch_detail.notes: Opens with roughly 50 ft of WI2 slab ice to a pool, followed by a WI3 curtain of 25-30 ft. Belay at a large boulder on climber's left at the top, equipped with webbing and a rap ring. Walk the rocky stream bed for about 100 ft to the next start.

pitch_detail.anchor: 2 pins with cord and a rap ring
pitch_detail.notes: Starts with about 20 ft of slab ice, then a 20-25 ft curtain, the best part of the route. The anchor is built from two pins joined with cord, plus a rap ring. Heavy snow can bury most of the route.

review.changed: 2 pitches written; lengths only given in feet, partly approximate, so omitted from lengthM.

pitch_detail.notes: Easy, enjoyable crack climbing up to a bit of loose rock; several large loose blocks could be dislodged. Once the crack ends, step right to a tree with low branches and belay there.
Offwidth moves lead to a loose jumble of blocks; go through carefully to a see-through flake, pass it and top out at a sturdy bush that serves as the belay.
Wander up a mostly unprotectable slab of solid rock and very easy climbing to a corner about 75 ft up, then to the roofs. Build a good belay on a mediocre ledge.
Traverse right under the roof, standing on small pebbles embedded in the rock, with excellent hand jams in the roof. Past the roof, belay on the ledge below the chimney.
Climb the chimney, which takes a #3.5 to #4 cam, then the arete on the left, moving onto the slab for a few face moves. Belay at a massive tree at the top and walk off.

review.changed: 3 pitches; P2 has no grade or length stated.

pitch_detail.notes: Scramble up a short ramp, then follow the line of bolts on sound rock to a belay on a thin ledge.

Traverse left 6 ft to a bolt, then go up steep rock past a rotten bulge to a stance on a strange spike under a large roof. Pull hard through the exposed roof to the slab above, where the belay is. If you fall at the roof it is hard to swing back to the rock, so prusiks may help.
A short pitch. Two bolts protect the slab up to a small left-facing corner; from there traverse right about 30 ft carefully to a bolted belay.
Grade is given as 5.9+ or 5.10a. Traverse left about 15 ft to 2 bolts, with more bolts higher leading to a fractured right-facing corner. Work up and right along it to a thin belay ledge.
Climb the dark water streak to easier ground, then past four more bolts (one hidden to the right around a rib) to a belay under a roof.
Traverse 35 ft straight left to a bolt, then pass a small tree and further bolts to a roomy top-out ledge with a single-bolt belay that can be backed up.

review.changed: 6 pitches. P4 grade is a range so kept in notes. First two pitches fully bolted, the rest need trad gear to supplement; lengths not given.
